scope.description: Scope control for the identity case: the same completion endpoint and the same re-synchronization, but with the caller's entry replicated to a quorum and adopted by the following leader.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum, in-process delivery under harness control
node 1's own entry is accepted by both followers while their receipts are dropped, so node 1 cannot decide
the two calls are judged by comparing the reported index against the entry actually decided there
excluded: how often the unadopted variant occurs in a deployment

basis.prefix: Same construction and transport as the executed revision (three real OmniPaxos instances over MemoryStorage warmed by omnipaxos_runtime actors from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; a pump task per node into a shared queue plus one delivery task that drops messages whose sender or receiver is isolated and, in the new case, messages of a listed (sender, receiver) pair). Case `append_notify_ok_for_entry_overwritten_at_that_index`: node 1 is isolated in both directions, accepts its own entry at index 1, node 2 takes over with an empty log and decides index 1 with its own entry, node 1 re-synchronizes and its call resolves Ok(1) while the entry there is node 2's. New case `ok_is_truthful_when_the_entry_is_adopted`: node 1 is leader; the pair (2,1) and (3,1) are dropped so both followers accept node 1's entry but node 1 never learns it (asserted a_decided_before == 0); node 2 takes over (`try_become_leader`), adopts the followers' log containing node 1's entry and decides index 1; the pairs are then released and node 1 is asked to reconnect, after which its call must resolve Ok(idx) with node 1's own entry at that index. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2000ms, egress_period 1ms, append_notify_timeout 30s.

before.description: Focused construction of one completion-endpoint identity case: an assigned index that is decided while the entry originally assigned to it was overwritten.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum, in-process delivery under harness control
node 1 isolated in both directions while node 2 takes over, so its entry cannot be adopted
node 1 re-admitted through the normal Promise + AcceptSync re-synchronization path
excluded: how often this interleaving occurs in a deployment

prefix.before: Unchanged from the previous version: three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) over MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; explicit transport (pump task per node into a shared queue, one delivery task popping and calling handle_incoming, dropping messages whose sender or receiver is isolated). Node 1 has leader_priority 10 and becomes leader after the initial heartbeats; node 1 is then isolated in both directions and `node1.append_notify(TestEntry(42))` is accepted locally at index 1 (read back as Undecided); `node2.try_become_leader()` makes node 2 the leader with node 3's promise and its own empty log, and `node2.append_notify(TestEntry(99))` is decided at index 1; node 1 is un-isolated and asked to reconnect, which makes it promise node 2 and receive an AcceptSync that truncates its log to node 2's and raises its decided index to 1. Emits CA_EVENT after_b_takeover {b_leader,c_leader,a_leader,b_decided,c_decided} (now JSON-safe strings) and CA_EVENT overwritten_index_resolution {a_decided_idx,a_entry_at_index_1_is_own,b_decided_idx,b_idx,resolution}, and asserts that the resolved call reports Ok(idx) while the entry at that index on node 1 is not the entry that call submitted. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2000ms, egress_period 1ms, append_notify_timeout 5s.

Case `append_notify_ok_for_entry_overwritten_at_that_index`: node 1 is isolated in both directions, accepts its own entry at index 1, node 2 takes over with an empty log and decides index 1 with its own entry, node 1 re-synchronizes and its call resolves Ok(1) while the entry there is node 2's. revision_reason: Adds one case (`ok_is_truthful_when_the_entry_is_adopted`) and one transport facility (a list of (sender, receiver) pairs whose messages are dropped); the existing case and its assertions are unchanged. The new case is the scope control for the windowed finding: node 1 accepts its own entry at index 1 while *both* followers' receipts are dropped, so node 1 stays at decided 0 with its call pending although a quorum accepted the entry; node 2 then takes over, adopts the followers' log (which contains node 1's entry), decides index 1, and node 1 re-synchronizes. The expectation from the adoption path (prepare-phase Promise log_sync / take_max_promise_sync) is that Ok(1) is then truthful, i.e. the entry at index 1 is node 1's own. Locally both cases pass in 4.0s: the new case emits adopted_entry_resolution {a_decided_before: 0, a_decided_idx: 1, a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: true, b_decided_idx: 1, resolution: "Ok(1)"} beside the windowed case's overwritten_index_resolution {..., a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: false, ..., resolution: "Ok(1)"}.
